description: Hand-maintained inputs to scripts/build-gazetteer.mjs. 'include' adds Natural Earth features that the default filters leave out, by dataset and ne_id. 'rename' replaces a Natural Earth name with its common English form before the ID is derived; renaming one feature to another's name merges them into the higher-ranked one. 'passages' gives marine features other than straits and channels a passage path, by ne_id; with 'between' ends a passage where it meets two named water bodies instead of at the ends of its long axis, and with 'junction' places a passage whose own polygon is unusable where two named water bodies meet, with a path through their water within radiusKm. 'canals' adds canals by their name in Natural Earth's river and lake centerlines; the joined centerline is the canal's passage path. 'features' adds the few features Natural Earth lacks; each is anchored to Natural Earth geometry, never to typed coordinates: a gazetteer place ('place'), the part of a country polygon containing a place ('countryPart'), the line where two marine polygons meet ('junction'), the middle of the shortest line between two region polygons ('narrows'), or the part of a marine polygon near where other water bodies meet it ('adjoining'). Keep every list short and give every entry a reason that names the geographic source.

include.name: Nagoya
include.reason: Japan coasts story names the Tokyo, Nagoya and Osaka corridor.

include.name: Memphis
include.reason: Waypoint on the Mississippi river route.

include.name: Kuantan
include.reason: East-coast port of Peninsular Malaysia; start of the route to Sabah.

include.name: Kota Kinabalu
include.reason: Capital and port of Sabah; end of the route from the peninsula.

include.name: French Guiana
include.reason: Overseas region of France; part of the FRA map identity, so not a country entry.

include.name: Punta Arenas
include.reason: Chile's port on the Strait of Magellan; the pilot's Chile and Argentina routes start or end there.

include.name: Cardiff
include.reason: Capital of Wales and its port on the Bristol Channel; the pilot's United Kingdom routes need a Welsh port.

include.name: Cape Breton Island
include.reason: Island on the south side of Cabot Strait; the strait's anchor.

rename.reason: Common English spelling; Natural Earth writes Tokyo without a macron.

One ID for the river. Natural Earth has it twice: the marine polygon 'Saint Lawrence River' (the estuary from Montreal to the gulf, with a passage path) and the river centerline 'St. Lawrence'. The same name merges them into the marine feature, which routes can follow.

passages.name: Gulf of Suez
passages.reason: Sea routes through the Suez Canal continue down the whole gulf to the Red Sea. The gulf bends, so a straight line from the canal to its label point crosses the Egyptian shore.

passages.name: Northwest Passage
passages.reason: Natural Earth's polygon covers the whole Arctic archipelago, whose long axis runs north to south. The passage runs from Lancaster Sound, where it meets Baffin Bay, to the Amundsen Gulf and the Beaufort Sea beyond.

passages.name: Gulf of Saint Lawrence
passages.reason: Ships cross the gulf between Cabot Strait and the Saint Lawrence River. Its label point lies east of Anticosti Island, so a straight line from it to the river crosses the island.

passages.name: Strait of Magellan
passages.reason: The strait bends sharply, so the ends of its long axis fall inside it, short of the Atlantic entrance at Cabo Virgenes. The passage runs from the Atlantic entrance to the Pacific one.

passages.name: Drake Passage
passages.reason: Natural Earth's Drake Passage polygon is seven slivers along the Antarctic shore, with no water to route through. The passage is where the Pacific and Atlantic polygons meet south of Cape Horn, so it is labelled at the middle of their shared boundary, with a path from the Pacific to the Atlantic through their water within 500 km of it.

canals.name: Suez Canal
canals.reason: Sea routes between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea pass through it. Natural Earth has it only as river and lake centerlines (scalerank 6), not as a marine polygon.

canals.name: Panama Canal
canals.reason: Sea routes between the Caribbean and the Pacific pass through it. Natural Earth has it only as river and lake centerlines (scalerank 6), not as a marine polygon.

features.name: Peninsular Malaysia
features.reason: Natural Earth has the whole Malay Peninsula, which extends into Thailand and Myanmar, but not Malaysia's peninsular region. Labelled at the interior point of the Malaysian polygon that contains Kuala Lumpur.

features.name: Cerrado
features.reason: Natural Earth has no biome features. The Cerrado savanna covers Brazil's central plateau, so it is labelled at Natural Earth's Planalto Central.

features.name: Strait of Hormuz
features.reason: Natural Earth's marine polygons have no Strait of Hormuz: the Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman polygons meet across it. Labelled at the middle of their shared boundary, with a passage from the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman through their water within 100 km of it.

features.name: Cabot Strait
features.reason: Natural Earth's Gulf of Saint Lawrence polygon runs past the strait to the open Atlantic, so there is no Cabot Strait feature. The strait is the narrowest water between Cape Breton Island and Newfoundland, so it is labelled at the middle of the shortest line between their Natural Earth region polygons.

features.name: Celtic Sea
features.reason: Natural Earth folds the Celtic Sea into the North Atlantic. It is the part of the Atlantic south of Ireland that the Irish Sea (through St George's Channel), the Bristol Channel and the English Channel open onto, so it is labelled at the interior point of the Atlantic's water within 150 km of where each of those three meets it.
